previous_description: Defines an input to an API operation by location, name, and schema. Parameters can appear in four locations: 'path' (always required, name must match the {placeholder} in the path template), 'query' (case-sensitive name, appended to the URL), 'header' (case-insensitive name), and 'cookie'. The 'schema' and 'content' attributes are mutually exclusive; 'content' requires exactly one map entry.
definition: A named input to an API operation or path item that is carried outside the request body, in the URL path, the query string, a request header or a cookie. It is identified by the pair (name, in) and constrained by either a schema or a single-entry content map.

distinguish_from.when: the input is carried in the HTTP message body, including form fields of application/x-www-form-urlencoded or multipart/form-data payloads.
the header describes a response header, or a multipart part header under an Encoding, where the name comes from a map key and no 'in' location is given.
the {placeholder} is substituted in a Server URL (host, base path, tenant) rather than in a Paths key template.
you are modelling the data type or constraints of the value itself rather than the named input slot that carries it.

code_evidence: Framework parameter bindings on handler arguments, such as Spring @PathVariable/@RequestParam/@RequestHeader/@CookieValue, FastAPI Path()/Query()/Header()/Cookie(), or ASP.NET [FromRoute]/[FromQuery]/[FromHeader].
Handler code reading req.params.<name>, req.query.<name>, req.get('<Header>') or req.cookies.<name> in an Express/Koa-style route registered on a router.
An entry under a 'parameters:' list in an OpenAPI YAML/JSON file, at operation, path-item or components level, containing 'name:' and 'in: path|query|header|cookie'.

attribute_descriptions.name: description
attribute_descriptions.description: Human-readable explanation of the parameter's meaning and accepted values, in CommonMark; set it whenever the name alone does not convey semantics or units.

attribute_descriptions.name: required
attribute_descriptions.description: Whether the client must supply the parameter. It must be true when in is 'path' and defaults to false otherwise; set it to true for mandatory query, header or cookie inputs.

attribute_descriptions.name: deprecated
attribute_descriptions.description: Marks the parameter as scheduled for removal so that consumers stop sending it. Defaults to false; set it to true when the handler still accepts the parameter but it is slated for removal.

attribute_descriptions.name: allowEmptyValue
attribute_descriptions.description: Permits a query parameter to be sent with an empty value (e.g. '?flag='). It is valid only when in is 'query', is ignored when style is set, and is discouraged in OpenAPI 3.0.3.

notes: The required OpenAPI 'name' field is missing, yet (name, in) forms the parameter's identity. The outgoing 'references' relationships to api.tag and api.operation look wrong: parameters do not reference tags, and operation→parameter already exists as an aggregates relationship. Also, 'example: any' sits uneasily beside the api.example relationship.
